paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when life is rough, you don't have to fake being fine. Psalm 123 is a song of ascents, and it's honest. The singer says his people have "endured much contempt" and asks for mercy twice (Psalm 123:3). Nobody in that song pretends, and the song never says the scorn stopped.

Now look at where their eyes go. They look to the LORD like servants looking to their master's hand, "until He shows us mercy" (Psalm 123:2). Then Psalm 124 is another song of ascents, this one of David, Israel's king, and he says that if the LORD had not been on their side, the floods would have engulfed them (Psalm 124:1, 4). I think the two songs sit well side by side, because one looks up and asks, and the other looks back and says thank You.

So what do you do with that, baker? You look UP, you ask, and then you tell somebody what He has done, because David wanted a whole crowd saying it with him. When you've slipped out of a snare, you say it out loud: "Our help is in the name of the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth" (Psalm 124:8). Whatever is on your plate today, keep your eyes on His hand, and keep a little room in your heart for the praise!
